items.title: A shared offer creates a reuse opportunity
items.summary: Observed: the homepage lists privacy, security, vendor and AI risk solutions.
items.implication: Inference: pilot reuse of context across those reviews, while retaining each discipline’s distinct decision and evidence requirements.

items.title: Investment context does not reveal current scale
items.summary: Observed: Vortex dates its investment to December 2017 and lists the holding as current.
items.implication: Inference: use the investment as company context only; revenue, staffing and present growth remain unknown.

items.title: An inventory supports more than register reporting
items.summary: Observed: the inventory page describes reusable processing information and import/export.
items.implication: Inference: owner attestations, provenance and change review should make reuse dependable across case and assessment work.

items.title: Contributor usability is an explicit product concern
items.summary: Observed: the assessment page describes DPIA Light for business contributors and connects assessment records.
items.implication: Inference: test occasional-user comprehension and factual completeness separately from specialist review quality.

items.title: Transfer review depends on processing context
items.summary: Observed: the TIA page connects transfer mechanisms, assessment records and reused processing context.
items.implication: Inference: keep the mechanism, evidence version and human transfer decision distinct; a completed assessment alone must not authorize a transfer.

items.title: Rights casework depends on data locations and controlled communications
items.summary: Observed: the request page describes identifying related processing, collaboration, optional masking and retention settings.
items.implication: Inference: preserve human review of scope and disclosure, and track whether the approved response was actually delivered.

items.title: Non-notification decisions also need evidence
items.summary: Observed: the breach-register page includes notification history and reasons not to notify.
items.implication: Inference: record awareness, responsibility and decision rationale; completion of a case must not imply that every incident required notification.

items.title: Security assurance needs a recurring operating cycle
items.summary: Observed: the ISMS page presents controls, risk assessment, review management and the PDCA cycle.
items.implication: Inference: model evidence freshness, failed tests and verified corrective actions alongside framework mappings.

items.title: Vendor assessment is a relationship lifecycle
items.summary: Observed: the third-party page describes centralized, customizable vendor assessment.
items.implication: Inference: anchor assessment scope to the intended supplier relationship and revisit it at material change, renewal and exit.

items.title: AI registers need ownership and a change history
items.summary: Observed: the AI Register page includes purpose, ownership, technical context and lifecycle documentation.
items.implication: Inference: link technical evaluation references and material changes to accountable reviews; do not imply the governance platform trains or monitors every model.

items.title: AI screening needs a reviewable boundary
items.summary: Observed: PrivacyPerfect offers AI pre-assessment and AI risk management. NIST describes its AI RMF as voluntary.
items.implication: Inference: record rule versions and uncertainty, and keep statutory applicability decisions separate from voluntary framework checks.

items.title: Partners define useful integration boundaries
items.summary: Observed: the partners page identifies filerskeepers for retention knowledge and Cookiebot for consent tooling.
items.implication: Inference: model approved information exchange and partner failure handling; do not assume a native consent engine or a particular connector protocol.

items.title: Activation and expansion are different buying moments
items.summary: Observed: the packages page lists free and paid options, allowances, add-ons and enterprise quotations.
items.implication: Inference: test initial activation independently from module expansion; verify current pricing and entitlements during contracting.

items.title: Entity hierarchy affects record visibility
items.summary: Observed: the FAQ distinguishes reusable tenant data from records governed by entity hierarchy and user roles.
items.implication: Inference: test entity moves, leavers and adviser access explicitly; reusable dictionaries must not become a route to disclosing case content.

items.title: Expert help is part of adoption
items.summary: Observed: the About page describes consultancy, training, support and customer success.
items.implication: Inference: treat training and handoffs as part of activation. A dedicated adviser delivery console is a proposed extension requiring discovery.

items.title: Rights channels must remain usable and accountable
items.summary: Observed: EDPB guidance calls for facilitating rights, clear responses and documentation, including reasons for not complying.
items.implication: Inference: preserve alternative intake routes, use proportionate clarification and evaluate clarity as well as elapsed response time.

items.title: Breach workflow must distinguish controller and processor responsibilities
items.summary: Observed: EDPB guidance distinguishes breach documentation, regulator notification conditions and processor escalation to the controller.
items.implication: Inference: capture the organization’s role and awareness event before choosing a workflow; avoid a universal notification timer for all incidents.
